title: A regular map factoring through a localization is regular from the localization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $W\subset A$ a multiplicative subset with localization map $\lambda:A\to W^{-1}A$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $\psi:W^{-1}A\to C$ a ring map. If the composite $\psi\circ\lambda:A\to C$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then $\psi$ is a regular ring map.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07PT (more-algebra-lemma-check-G-ring-maximal-ideals, line 12392), sentence 'Since it factors through the localization R_p, also the ring map R_p -> (R_m^)_{p'}^ is regular', stated without proof; flatness: algebra.tex Lemma Tag 00HT (2) (lemma-flat-localization); primes of W^{-1}A: algebra.tex Lemma Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization)

proof.text: Unfold RingHom.IsRegular and normalize algebraMap.toAlgebra. Flatness over A follows from the first conjunct of hpsi. Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization A\prime W C gives flatness over A\prime.

For a prime q\prime of A\prime, contraction q is prime by Ideal.IsPrime.comap. A localization map is surjective on stalks (RingHom.surjectiveOnStalks_of_isLocalization), so its canonical residue-field map is bijective (RingHom.SurjectiveOnStalks.residueFieldMap_bijective). AlgEquiv.ofBijective gives an A-algebra isomorphism sigma: kappa(q) to kappa(q\prime). No prime-ideal correspondence or local-ring comparison theorem is needed.

Tensor sigma with the identity on C using Algebra.TensorProduct.congr. The localization gives IsLocalization.tensorProduct_compatibleSMul; Algebra.TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul identifies kappa(q\prime) tensor_A C with kappa(q\prime) tensor_A\prime C. Composing gives the fibre-ring isomorphism. Tensor induction proves its compatibility with sigma on residue-field scalars (zero and sums by additivity; pure tensors by map_mul and scalar multiplication).

The composite map supplies geometric regularity of q.Fiber C. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-field-iso] to sigma and the compatible fibre-ring isomorphism to obtain geometric regularity of q\prime.Fiber C. Together with flatness, this is exactly RingHom.IsRegular for algebraMap A\prime C.
